- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; cap upward revisions to prevent overshoot.  
- If 30-day forecast shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecast peaks then drops), reduce early peaks and smooth transitions.  
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to underreact to sentiment shifts — apply a 1-2 day lag correction to align with sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows rising trend, forecast should trend upward; if falling, forecast should trend downward — don’t ignore sentiment direction.  
- Don’t forecast beyond 10% above or below 30-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.
